summary: API gateway fallback throttling leading to slow 5xx growth and intermittent runtime crashes
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (notably BrightForms) started seeing a gradual but persistent increase in 5xx responses from text-generation endpoints beginning ~2026-03-12 05:10 UTC. Error rate climbed from baseline ~0.2% to ~3% over an hour, with periodic spikes to 8-12% correlated with tenant connection failovers and streaming route fallbacks. Some calls observed upstream runtime exits (OOM and SIGABRT) during the same window.

Impact:
- BrightForms reported degraded product experience for ~15% of requests that route through the us-east dedicated pool.
- Increased token replays and customer-visible latency due to retries.
- Potential billing concerns for duplicate/hedged requests.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east-1), Dedicated capacity cluster for BrightForms (tenant id bfrm-1182).
- API route: /v1/chat/completions (streaming and non-streaming).
- Model variants: redwood-open-13b (quantized), mosaic-ml-7b (fallback variant).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run a sustained low-latency stream workload with ~600 rps (mix of streaming and short non-streaming).
2) Simulate occasional socket hiccups by introducing short (100-300ms) packet drops at the proxy layer.
3) Observe that traffic migrates to fallback routes and throttler engages after connection churn.
4) Monitor apigw 5xx rate and runtime watcher logs for OOM/SIGABRT.
comments: 2026-03-12 05:30 UTC - Support (Aisha): Initial triage - elevated 5xx for BrightForms, escalated to SRE. Captured request ids and sample stack traces. Notified customer of investigation.

2026-03-12 05:45 UTC - SRE (Marco): Observed accept-queue growth on apigw frontends and increased fallback routing to secondary runtime pool. Several runtime processes logged low-memory OOM messages around 05:20-05:40 UTC.

2026-03-12 06:10 UTC - Eng (Priya - serving-runtime): Hypothesis - throttler/backoff policy on fallback path incorrectly uses aggregated pending-requests count (includes hedged retry attempts) which amplified queueing under connection churn, causing runtime preemption and increased memory pressure.

2026-03-12 06:35 UTC - Support (Aisha): Sent workaround to BrightForms: reduced client-side concurrent streams and temporarily pinned calls to primary variant (redwood-open-13b) to avoid fallback fanout. Customer confirmed partial improvement.
2026-03-12 07:05 UTC - SRE (Marco): Applied temporary apigw throttling adjustment for BrightForms route (raise soft limit, increase keepalive). Observed 5xx drop from 3% -> 0.6% over 20 minutes.
2026-03-12 09:20 UTC - Eng (Priya): Deployed a hotfix to throttle logic to exclude hedged/retry in pending count calculations (canary 5 nodes). Monitoring for regressions.
2026-03-12 12:00 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer reports stable behavior with occasional blips. Keeping ticket open for follow-up and postmortem.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 05:10 UTC: first customer alerts and SLO alarms.
- 05:15-05:40 UTC: accept-queue on apigw frontends for tenant bfrm-1182 rose by 6x; fallback traffic to secondary pool increased by 4x.
- 05:20-05:42 UTC: runtime logs show repeated 'std::bad_alloc' / OOM killer entries on 3/12 nodes, followed by abrupt restarts.
- 05:30 UTC: hedged retry rate increased after client reconnects, leading to duplicate inflight requests counted by throttler.

Findings:
- Throttler uses an aggregate inflight counter that included hedged/replicated attempts. Under connection churn this inflated perceived concurrency and triggered aggressive backoff that propagated to fallback routing.
- Fallback routing increased model fanout (calls to multiple variant pools) which raised memory allocation peaks in runtimes not prewarmed for the extra concurrency.
- Keepalive/session churn on apigw compounded the problem by forcing cold rehandshakes and transient request spikes.

Evidence:
- apigw metric (apigw.accept_queue.depth) spike graph (link in related_confluence_pages).
- Runtime logs: /var/log/redwood/runtime/watcher.log entries referencing OOM and SIGABRT (sample ids attached in incident folder).
- Correlation between hedged.retry.rate and 5xx_rate (Pearson r=0.82 for 05:10-06:00 UTC).
resolution:
Actions taken:
1) Immediate: Raised apigw soft accept limits and increased keepalive durations for the BrightForms route to reduce connection churn (mitigated within 20 minutes).
2) Hotfix: Adjusted throttler logic to exclude hedged/retry attempts from inflight counters; canary deployed and validated on 9 nodes, then rolled to remaining frontends. (github.com/redwood-inference/apigw/pull/1309)
3) Runtime stabilization: Restarted three affected runtime processes with larger prewarm pools and applied a memory allocation cap to guard against single-tenant preemption.
4) Customer remediation: Provided guidance to BrightForms to reduce their concurrent stream count temporarily (and option to increase dedicated capacity).
5) Follow-up actions:
   - Postmortem scheduled (owner: Priya Shah) to analyze root cause and long-term fix.
   - Add unit/integration tests to throttler to prevent counting hedged retries.
   - Add alerting to detect sudden hedged-retry amplification and fallback fanout (owner: SRE).

Status: mitigated; monitoring for recurrence. Customer notified and satisfied with interim remediation; ticket will be closed after postmortem and permanent fix deployment.
